comparison: Both evaluate methodological details and survey data (C1-C3, C73, C79-C84). OpenEval finds the data comprehensive and well-documented (SUPPORTED), while peer reviewers express uncertainty due to 'very little information presented' and concerns about data quality and methodological detail (UNCERTAIN). Major disagreement on data adequacy.

Both assess species-specific responses (C4-C18). OpenEval finds statistical results clearly presented with appropriate uncertainty quantification (SUPPORTED), while peer reviewers criticize models as 'simplistic' with only linear predictors, no interactions, and lacking ecological perspective (UNCERTAIN). Significant methodological disagreement.

Both evaluate human modification effects on co-occurrence (C19-C24, C37, C95). OpenEval finds patterns coherent and well-supported by figures (SUPPORTED), while peer reviewers identify fundamental problems: study not set up to test interaction between disturbance and co-occurrence, lacks distinction between significant and random associations (UNCERTAIN). Core methodological disagreement.

Both assess human presence effects (C25-C30, C38). OpenEval finds patterns consistent and well-supported (SUPPORTED), while peer reviewers raise same concerns as R3 about lacking proper statistical framework for testing interactions and distinguishing significant associations (UNCERTAIN). Parallel disagreement to human modification results.

Both evaluate temporal niche responses (C31-C34, C117). OpenEval finds guild-specific responses well-supported with appropriate statistics (SUPPORTED), while peer reviewers question why temporal variables weren't included as interaction terms with niche predictors and human disturbance (UNCERTAIN). Methodological concern about testing temporal niche hypotheses.

Both assess reduced encounter times (C35-C36, C39, C96, C116). OpenEval finds results well-supported with visual confirmation (SUPPORTED), while peer reviewers accept the statistical result but doubt the mechanistic interpretation due to lack of proper interaction terms and incomplete evidence (UNCERTAIN). Pattern observed but causal interpretation disputed.

Both evaluate main ecological conclusions (C40-C41, C93-C94, C97, C103, C120, C125, C140-C141). OpenEval finds core findings well-supported though some claims are appropriately qualified (SUPPORTED), while peer reviewers explicitly state incomplete evidence for claims about positive interactions, note discussion adds little, and question advance in ecological understanding (UNSUPPORTED). Strongest disagreement on overall conclusions.

Both discuss threshold patterns (C109-C110). OpenEval finds non-linear threshold pattern reasonable given the data (SUPPORTED), while peer reviewers acknowledge the threshold concept but express uncertainty due to methodological concerns about interaction terms and incomplete evidence (UNCERTAIN). Partial overlap with C113 in OpenEval only.

Both evaluate JSDM methodology (C91-C92). OpenEval finds approach well-established and appropriate (SUPPORTED), while peer reviewers state JSDM is 'in principle, a nice way' but raise critical concerns about spatial autocorrelation treatment and mismatch between hypotheses and methods (UNCERTAIN). Agreement on principle, disagreement on implementation.

Partial overlap on study contribution (C99). OpenEval finds contextualization appropriate (SUPPORTED), while peer reviewers question the advance in ecological understanding as part of broader methodological critique (UNCERTAIN). OpenEval also covers C107-C108 not addressed by peer reviewers.
OpenEval evaluates covariate selection and measurement (C85-C90) as well-documented and appropriate (SUPPORTED). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological details.
OpenEval finds human presence documentation (C122-C124) supported by detection data and citations (SUPPORTED). No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval rates extrapolations to ecological consequences (C129-C138) as uncertain, noting claims about fitness, extinction, disease transmission are not directly measured and are speculative (UNCERTAIN). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer concerns about incomplete evidence align with this assessment.
OpenEval rates conservation recommendations (C143-C144) as uncertain, noting they go beyond what data directly support (UNCERTAIN). No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval finds literature context and citations (C42-C72, C74-C78, C98, C100-C106, C111-C112, C114-C115, C118-C119, C121, C126-C128, C139, C142) appropriate for established knowledge (SUPPORTED). No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval finds methodological conclusion about camera trap feasibility (C145) reasonable given successful application (SUPPORTED). No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
